name: an embedding is unread like an override, subjects fold compatibility digits, rejected merchant text scores 0
notes: §11 (v1.3): a string holding a bidi override or embedding (U+202A, U+202B, U+202D, U+202E) yields no subject tokens and no name tokens; bidi marks and isolates (and the terminator U+202C) are only stripped. Subjects fold compatibility digits with NFKC deliberately (Q³ → q3). §5.1 (v1.3) merchantMatch: merchant text is read through counterparty(); text it rejects has no name tokens (claim: not applicable; observation: 0). v1.2 named only the overrides, so an embedding was stripped like a mark. Invisible characters are written as JSON \u escapes.

receiptMerchants is patched to ['acme'], so 'acme' purchases are fully covered. One gmail.sent and one gmail.receipt entry (acct-a, the only account hash) saw [09:00, 19:00] and synced 19:00 = evaluatedAt, so every claim is past grace (19:00 ≥ each end + 45). The grant has no ceiling and no allowlist. Pairs are two hours apart, so each observation is only in its own claim's window.

c1 priya@company.com 'Q3 deck' (10:02) × o1 priya@company.com 'Q3 <U+202B RIGHT-TO-LEFT EMBEDDING>deck<U+202C>': applicable timeProximity 2500, counterpartyExact 3500, counterpartyDomain 1500, subjectOverlap 1500; Σw = 9000. tp 1, ce 1, cd 1 (company.com is not common); the observation subject holds an embedding → no tokens → subjectOverlap 0 (an observation with no tokens scores 0). S = 7500/9000 = 5/6 ≥ 1/2 and < 17/20 → partial, FINAL. Stripping the embedding (the v1.2 reading) would read {q3, deck} → 1/1 VERIFIED.

c2 raj@company.com 'Q3 deck' (12:02) × o2 raj@company.com 'Q<U+00B3 SUPERSCRIPT THREE> deck': NFKC folds ³ to 3 → {q3, deck} → subjectOverlap 1 → S = 9000/9000 = 1/1 → verified, FINAL. Treating the superscript as unread (the rule for amounts, times and names) would give no tokens → 5/6 PARTIAL; not folding it would give {q³, deck} → Jaccard 1/3 → 8/9.

c3 'Pri<U+202A LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING>ya' (a name, no '@') 'Q3 deck' (14:02): the name holds an embedding → no name tokens → counterpartyName not applicable; it is not an address, so counterpartyExact is not applicable either → no email.sent identity feature → underspecified (§5.2): UNVERIFIABLE, claim.too_vague, FINAL at once, never scored (match.none). o3 priya@company.com in its window is never compared with it and, with no activity, is an orphan with no receipt. Stripping the embedding would read 'priya' → counterpartyName 1 → 1/1 VERIFIED.

c4 purchase 'acme' 3000 USD (16:02) × o4 receipt 'Ac<U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE>me' 3000 USD: applicable timeProximity 2500, amountExact 2500, merchantMatch 2000 (the claim's 'acme' is readable; no subject); Σw = 7000. tp 1, amountExact 1; the observation's merchant is text counterparty() rejects → merchantMatch 0. S = 5000/7000 = 5/7 → partial, FINAL (graceElapsed). Stripping the override would read 'acme' = 'acme' → 1/1 VERIFIED.

c5 purchase 'Ac<U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE>me' 3000 USD (18:02) × o5 receipt 'Acme Store' 3000 USD: the claim's merchant text is rejected → merchantMatch not applicable (the claim decides applicability, §5.2); amountExact is applicable, so not underspecified. Applicable timeProximity 2500, amountExact 2500; Σw = 5000; tp 1, amountExact 1 → S = 1/1 → verified, FINAL (19:00 ≥ end(18:03) + 30). Whether name() of the rejected text is in receiptMerchants does not matter: verified fires before any coverage rule except no_coverage, and the receipt interval overlaps the window. Reading the text with the override stripped would make merchantMatch applicable: Jaccard {acme} vs {acme, store} = 1/2 → 6/7; scoring it 0 would give 5/7 PARTIAL.
